answer: Because the mirror stake is held until the wharf settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the kernel audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 38% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A farm running 28 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
